issues.description: Renders from only fold angles 0 (r1) and 90 (r9) were kept; sweep revisions r2-r8 were built without renders. Rendering at a second angle needed `cad set` then `cad render`, which creates a new revision each time.
`cad measure --thickness` prints a long list of sample points rather than a single minimum, so the minimum is hard to read at a glance.

Unclear whether sweep's 'closest' line reports only the single closest pair or checks every pair; the output only names arm<->base_block even though the forearm is the moving part, so it is hard to see the forearm was checked.
measure --thickness includes the wall around holes in the base, which the task did not require, and it gives no per-part pass/fail threshold flag.
Docs don't say whether 'at least 0.5 mm' passes at exactly 0.5; I used 1.0 mm gaps to be safe.
Rotation sign for swinging a downward-pointing link toward +X needs a negative angle about Y; the docs state the rule but I had to derive the sign myself.
XZ-plane extrude offset/distance sign convention (offset=-y0, negative distance) is non-obvious; the doc example helped.
cad sweep renders are written into per-revision dirs (r2..r13) and clutter the project; no way to name or collect them.
XZ plane offset/extrude sign (offset=d -> Y=-d, positive distance -> -Y) is easy to get wrong; my first base_mount landed at Y -4..2 and overlapped the upper link until I checked bbox.
Rotating the lower link: positive rotation about y turns -Z toward -X, so the knee needed rotate(-knee). Docs state the rule but a worked example of a hanging link would help.
Shell sandbox rejected heredoc writes to files and commands containing dict braces with quotes; had to use the Write tool.
Sign convention for swinging a -Z-pointing link toward +X (rotate about y by -angle) had to be reasoned out and verified via hole positions.
Docs don't say how to model 'touch but not intrude'; I cut an equal-diameter cylinder Part, giving exact tangent contact. Clearance reports contact correctly.
cad clearance lists reference-vs-reference pairs (cable/sensor touching) which is noise.

Reference envelopes that deliberately share space (sensor body vs lift-out volume) are reported as 'overlap' by cad clearance, which is noisy; no way to mark reference-vs-reference pairs as ignorable.
No dedicated contact check for a cut seat touching the sensor; I had to read the clearance output (it showed 'touching', which worked).
Reference-envelope clearance output is verbose; hard to see at a glance that the 6 mm screw-head paths and 7 mm shaft column are clear (no way to declare keep-out columns).
I did not visually inspect the PNG renders (only generated them); verification relied on numeric checks (clearance, thickness, holes).
Doc does not say whether the 7 mm shaft column starts at the servo top (Z=50) or extends from Z=0; I kept the whole column above Z=50 clear.
No built-in check for a vertical screw-head path (6 mm cylinder above a hole) or a shaft column against all parts. I checked it by hand from the coordinates.
Reference box clearance output is long and per-face. It was useful for the 0.5 mm side gaps, but a pass/fail summary line would help.
No visible way to make a hole's ligament check ignore pilot holes; I had to size the clamp plate by trial (2.8 mm ligament at first) using measure --thickness.

Cutting a hex pocket from the bottom face needed extrude with plane XY offset=-12 and positive distance (going +Z); the docs' offset/normal table made this derivable but there is no 'pocket' helper for polygon pockets.
No direct check that a hex pocket's flats are parallel to X or its across-flats size; I relied on the construction (angle=0 gives flats at v=±AF/2).
Shell redirection (heredoc) to create model.py was blocked by the sandbox; had to use a file-write tool. Not a cad issue.

For a 3D hole start point, it was not obvious whether depth is measured from that point; I had to try it and check cad measure --holes. Also unclear that a hole starting exactly on a face needs the 3D form.
No direct check that two parts do not intersect or touch only at a plane (e.g. interference volume); I relied on construction.

suggestions.suggestion: Print the minimum wall thickness as a summary line in `cad measure --thickness`.
Allow `cad render --param fold_angle=90` without modifying params.toml.
Have `cad measure --holes` show hole axis positions in assembly frame consistently (all holes were listed).
Make cad sweep print the minimum gap for every pair at every value, not just the closest pair.
Add a convenience for a link/slot with pivot holes (stadium plate with end holes).
Add a clear note in the docs that a part's rotate() after translate() works about a world-frame centre.
Sweep output could list min clearance per part pair at every step, not just the closest pair.
Parameter defaults could be shown in `cad docs` next to hole_pattern example with a plate-corner-at-origin case (center=(w/2,h/2)).
A Part.hole_pattern/grid helper for rectangular hole arrays would avoid the manual loop.
Allow shell heredoc file creation, or document that Write is the way to author model.py.
Let hole_pattern accept center='part' (or default to the part bbox centre) so the pattern centring doesn't need a manual plate_width/2 expression.
Add a 'revolute link' example (slot-shaped link with pivot holes, Y-layered) to cad examples.
Let cad sweep write its renders to a named folder.
Report clearance sweeps as the minimum across all pairs, not only the closest pair.
Add an assembly example with a hinged link and layered Y slabs.
cad sweep could print the foot/hole positions per angle to verify the kinematics.
Show part Y-range in build summary.
Add a worked example of an articulated two-link assembly with a motion parameter
Let sweep report per-pair minimum gaps, not only the closest pair
Allow cut() with a reference Part directly
Support keep-out boxes as references and flag any intersection
Option to ignore reference-vs-reference pairs in cad clearance
Allow excluding pairs in cad clearance (e.g. ignore reference-vs-reference pairs).
Add a 'keep-out' reference kind for regions that must stay empty.
A keep-out volume check (reference part for the lift-out region) would let clearance verify the 'nothing above mid-plane' requirement directly.
Allow reference keep-out volumes (e.g. screw-head columns) with a cad clearance check against them.
Warn when a clearance 'touching' pair is intentional versus contact on a side face.
Add a `cad clearance`-style check for keep-out cylinders or columns defined as reference parts, with a pass/fail result.
Document the hole-ligament thickness behaviour of `--thickness` (it reported 2.8 mm for a hole near a plate edge, which was helpful).
Add a worked example of an envelope-based bracket with a removable clamp plate.
Let cad clearance take a per-pair expectation, e.g. contact allowed only on named faces.
Add a pocket(profile, depth, face=...) helper or polygon pocket option on hole().
Report non-circular pockets in measure --holes.
Add a built-in way to check that a hex pocket's flats are parallel to a given axis (e.g. query on planar face normals grouped by direction).
Add `cad interference` reporting overlap volume between parts and contact area.
Document the hex orientation for regular_polygon in a worked nut-pocket example.
